action: Create a Cube in the scene.
notes: Used as a visual reference while creating the skeleton.

action: Create and draw out a skeleton.
notes: Creates the skeleton points for the FK rig.

action: Keep the default skeleton point names unchanged.
notes: The points retain their default names, such as 0, 1 and 2.

action: Create a Pack Folder node.
Connect the skeleton to the second input of the Pack Folder.
notes: Packs the skeleton into the folder.

action: Change the Pack Folder type to Skeleton.
notes: Changes the packed component type.

action: Set the skeleton's name to Base.
notes: Follows the default naming convention used by the Auto Rig Component.

action: Create an Auto Rig Component node.
Set the Auto Rig Component name to FK.
Open the Component dropdown and select FK.
Locate the Transform promotion group parameter.
notes: T represents translation/transform.

action: Locate the Rotation promotion group parameter.
notes: R represents rotation.

action: Locate the Scale promotion group parameter.
notes: S represents scale.

action: Enter * as the wildcard for the promotion group fields.
keys_or_menu: T Promote Group / R Promote Group / S Promote Group
notes: Selects all skeleton points for transform, rotation and scale promotion.

action: Use the wildcard to include all points in the rig.
Identify the common naming pattern of the skeleton points.
notes: The instructor explains that the points share a common naming convention.

action: Replace the general wildcard with point* to target points with the Point naming prefix.
notes: A more specific alternative to *.

action: Apply the FK component configuration.
notes: Generates the FK controls for the selected points.

action: Open the Configure Controls functionality.
Create a separate Configure Controls node.
notes: The instructor recommends using the standalone node.

action: Compare the Configure Controls options available in the Auto Rig Component with those in the standalone node.
notes: The standalone node exposes additional dropdown options.

action: Inspect the Shape Override options available in the standalone Configure Controls node.
notes: The instructor explains that the embedded configuration has fewer options.

action: Use the standalone Configure Controls node instead of relying on the embedded Auto Rig Component configuration.
notes: Recommended because it provides more customization options.

action: Set the Control Group field to point*.
notes: Targets all points following the Point naming convention.

action: Set Shape Override to Box.
notes: Changes the appearance of the FK controls.

action: Enable Use Shape Offset.
notes: Allows the control shape to be adjusted independently.

action: Increase the shape offset scale values to 4.1.
notes: Your notes record 4.1 for each scale value.

action: Enable Use Color.
Choose a color for the FK controls.
notes: The instructor selects a color.

action: Create an Add Character node.
notes: Adds the character to the APEX evaluation scene.

action: Connect the Configure Controls output to the Add Character node.
Create an Animate node.
Connect the Add Character output to the Animate node.
Inspect the generated FK controls in the Animate node.
notes: Confirms that the character has FK control.

action: Introduce a spider-like creature as an example of modifying the skeleton.
notes: Demonstrates how APEX supports changes to the skeleton.

action: Return to the skeleton and select it for modification.
Press F to enter Modify mode.
Select a skeleton point and move it to adjust the skeleton shape.
Select another skeleton point to modify the structure.
notes: The instructor changes the selected point before continuing.

action: Create a Merge node to combine the skeletons.
Connect the skeletons to the Merge node.
notes: Combines the skeleton geometry so the changes can be viewed together.

action: Move the first skeleton section to a different position.
Move the second skeleton section to a different position.
notes: Creates the additional skeleton sections for the spider-like example.

action: Create or use a Pack Folder to pack the merged skeleton geometry.
Connect the merged skeleton geometry to the Pack Folder.
Set the Pack Folder type to Skeleton.
notes: Maintains the correct component type.

action: Re-enter the skeleton name in the Pack Folder.
notes: The name is lost when the packed geometry is deselected and reconnected.

action: Check the existing FK component after modifying the skeleton.
notes: The previous FK setup no longer works correctly because the point names are no longer unique.

action: Identify the duplicate point names in the merged skeleton.
notes: The merged skeleton contains naming conflicts, such as repeated point indices.

action: Create an Attribute Wrangle node.
notes: Used to generate unique joint names.

action: Open the Attribute Wrangle code editor.
Enter a naming expression that assigns a jnt_ prefix to each point name.
notes: s@name = "jnt_" + itoa(@ptnum);

action: Use the itoa() function to convert the point number from an integer into a string.
notes: Allows the point number to be appended to the joint-name prefix.

action: Apply the expression to generate unique names for the skeleton points.
notes: Prevents duplicate naming conflicts in the merged skeleton.

action: Return to the FK component and inspect the updated skeleton.
notes: The FK component updates automatically when the skeleton changes.

action: Identify that the FK controls are not working correctly because the naming convention has changed.
notes: The FK component still references the old Point naming pattern.

action: Change the skeleton point naming convention to use the joint prefix.
notes: The intended naming pattern is now based on jnt_ names.

action: Inspect the skeleton and verify that FK controls are generated for the renamed joints.
Open the standalone Configure Controls node and change the Control Group from point to joint.
notes: Updates the control selection to match the new naming convention.

action: Apply the updated Configure Controls settings to generate controls for all joints.
Open the Animate node and test the FK controls on the modified skeleton.
notes: Confirms that the modified skeleton can be animated using FK controls.

action: Introduce the next tutorial topic: creating a basic arm IK rig.
notes: The actual arm IK setup is not included in this tutorial.
